hostControl.intro: Manage the printer's Linux host - check its health, control its background services, free disk space, and change system settings (time, locale, hostname, network, power).

steps: Read the cards for CPU temperature, memory, disk and network at a glance.
Watch the top-processes table to see what is using the CPU right now.
Leave auto-refresh on for a live view, or turn it off and refresh manually.

monitor.title: Reading the monitor
monitor.body: Everything here is read-only. Bars turn amber past 75% and red past 90%. CPU temperature turns amber at 70 °C and red at 80 °C. The throttle warning only appears on boards that report it (mainly Raspberry Pi).

services.title: Managing services
services.body: Each row is a systemd service. Click one to start/stop/restart it, enable/disable it at boot, mask it, read its log, or - for services you installed yourself - delete its unit file. Stopping or disabling a service takes a typed or one-tap confirmation. Critical and protected services are marked; protected ones (like SSH and this panel) can't be stopped, to avoid locking you out.

cleanup.title: Freeing disk space
cleanup.body: Each row is scanned first to show how much it would free. Tick the ones to clear and confirm. Only regenerable data is offered - the apt download cache, old systemd journal, ~/.cache, your old /tmp files, and rotated (non-live) logs. Your G-code, timelapses and configs are never touched.

system.title: System settings
system.body: Change the host's timezone and clock, language and keyboard, hostname or network (DHCP / static IP), or reboot/shut it down. Each change applies immediately. Reboot and shutdown are refused while a print is running. Changing the IP may briefly drop your connection to this panel.

network.title: DHCP vs Static IP
network.body: DHCP (auto) lets your router assign the address automatically. Static (manual) pins a fixed address - set the IP, subnet (CIDR, e.g. /24), gateway (usually your router) and DNS. IPv4 only. Changing the address of the connection that serves this panel will drop your session; reconnect at the new IP. A wrong static address or gateway can make the printer unreachable until you fix it on the device itself, so the settings are validated and need a typed confirmation.

canbus.title: CAN bus setup
canbus.body: A CAN bus links the host to your toolhead/MCU boards over two wires (CANH and CANL). Three rules make it work: every board has a unique UUID that goes in your printer config; every node must run the SAME bitrate; and the bus needs exactly two 120Ω terminators, one at each physical end. 1 Mbit/s (1000000) is the standard rate. After wiring, bring the interface up and confirm the controller reads ERROR-ACTIVE and your MCUs connect. A board that does not show up is most often already claimed in your config (normal) or running a different bitrate.

canParams.title: Bitrate & advanced parameters
canParams.body: The bitrate is fixed in each board's firmware (and its bootloader) - changing it here on the host alone takes every CAN MCU offline. Only change it after reflashing every board to the same new speed. Lower rates (500k/250k) add margin on a long or noisy bus, but only once wiring and termination are correct, and they reduce bandwidth - so they make a saturation problem worse, not better. Leave Sample point and SJW blank: the kernel then picks the recommended ~87.5% sample point for you; set them only as an expert override. TX queue length should be 128 (raise it only with 5+ MCUs on one bus; much larger values add latency and can cause errors). Auto-restart of 0 keeps it off; ~100 ms self-recovers from a bus-off, but if the bus keeps dropping, fix the wiring instead of relying on it. Keep every control-mode flag OFF for normal printing - Listen-only and One-shot in particular stop the host acknowledging or retrying frames and make the MCUs unreachable.

canTermination.title: 120Ω termination & troubleshooting
canTermination.body: Terminate exactly two nodes - the two physical ends of the bus; any node in the middle must have its 120Ω terminator OFF. To check it, power the printer OFF and measure across CANH/CANL: about 60Ω is correct (two terminators in parallel), ~120Ω means only one is fitted, ~40Ω means three, and an open reading means none. Twist CANH and CANL together, keep the run short and away from stepper, heater and mains wiring, and make sure the toolhead connectors cannot shake loose (motion is the top cause of intermittent errors). Reading the bus: ERROR-ACTIVE is healthy; ERROR-PASSIVE, BUS-OFF, or climbing error counters point to termination, wiring, or a bitrate mismatch - check those in that order.

host.def: The small Linux computer (e.g. a Raspberry Pi or BTT CB1) that runs Klipper, Moonraker and FilaMind - separate from the printer's microcontrollers.

load.def: How many processes were waiting to run, averaged over 1 / 5 / 15 minutes. Roughly: a value near the core count means the CPU is busy; well above it means it is overloaded.

swap.def: Disk space used as overflow when RAM fills up. Heavy swap use slows the host down - a sign it is short on memory.

throttle.def: When the board reduces speed to protect itself - usually from an under-powered supply (under-voltage) or overheating. Reported mainly on Raspberry Pi.

ntp.def: Network Time Protocol keeps the host clock accurate. An unsynced clock can break timelapses, logs and TLS certificates.

locale.def: The host's language and keyboard layout settings, used by the OS for text, dates and the console keymap.

service.def: A background program managed by systemd - Klipper, Moonraker, the webcam streamer and the network stack all run as services.

enabled.def: Whether a service starts automatically at boot. 'enabled' starts on boot; 'disabled' doesn't; 'static' is only started by another service.

mask.def: A stronger form of disable - the service can't be started at all (even by another service) until it's unmasked. Use with care.

canbus.def: A two-wire (CANH/CANL) network linking the host to toolhead and MCU boards, so a toolhead needs only a few wires instead of a full loom.

uuid.def: A unique factory identifier for each CAN board. You put it in your printer config so the host knows which board is which.

bitrate.def: The CAN signalling speed in bits per second (1000000 = 1 Mbit/s is standard). It is set in each board's firmware; the host and every node must use the same value.

samplePoint.def: Where in each bit the signal level is read (~87.5% is standard). Leave it blank and the kernel sets it correctly for the chosen bitrate.

sjw.def: Sync Jump Width - how far the controller may shift its timing per bit to stay in sync. Leave blank unless you have a clock-tolerance issue; it cannot exceed the controller's limit.

termination.def: A resistor at each of the two bus ends (about 60Ω measured across CANH/CANL with power off). Exactly two are needed; middle nodes must have theirs off.

busoff.def: The controller removed itself from the bus after too many errors - usually wrong termination, wiring, or a bitrate mismatch. It needs a restart, and the underlying fault fixed.

txqueuelen.def: How many CAN packets Linux buffers for sending. 128 is recommended; much larger values add latency and can cause unrecoverable errors.

services.warning: Stopping or disabling the wrong service can take the printer offline. Critical services are marked; protected ones can't be stopped.
services.deleteFailed: Could not remove the unit file.
services.deletePrompt: This permanently removes the unit file. Type "{name}" to confirm.

cleanup.subtitle: Tick what to remove, then clean. Caches and old logs only - prints and configs stay safe.

apt.label: Package cache
apt.desc: Downloaded .deb installer files apt no longer needs.

journal.label: System journal
journal.desc: Old systemd logs - vacuumed down to the most recent 50 MB.

tmp.label: Temp files
tmp.desc: Your own files in /tmp older than a day.

logs.label: Rotated logs
logs.desc: Old, rotated Klipper/Moonraker logs (the live log is kept).

system.manualTimeHint: Turn off automatic time to set the clock by hand.
system.hostnameHint: Letters, digits and hyphens only. Takes full effect after a reboot.
system.powerWarning: Reboot and shutdown are refused while a print is running.
system.needsSetup: This action needs passwordless sudo. On the printer, run: sudo bash scripts/install.sh sudoers - then retry.

boot.intro: How the host boots: the default target and the boot splash. Read-only here; changing the splash comes later.
boot.noSplash: No boot splash found on this host.
boot.changeHint: Changing the boot splash + a design studio are coming in a later update.

studio.title: Design the boot splash
studio.failed: Could not apply the boot splash.
studio.caveat: Writes a PNG to the boot-splash path; whether it shows at boot depends on your host's splash setup.

canbus.intro: View and manage the host's CAN bus interfaces: link state, bitrate and error counters. Reads are safe; changes need passwordless sudo and are refused while printing.
canbus.warn: Changing CAN settings affects every MCU on the bus. Never do it during a print.
canbus.none: No CAN interfaces found on this host.
canbus.confirmDown: Bringing the bus down disconnects every CAN MCU until it is back up. Continue?
canbus.downFirst: Bring the interface down to change its bitrate.
canbus.restartHint: Recover a controller that has gone BUS-OFF.
canbus.noiseHint: Triple sampling and a higher SJW improve tolerance to electrical noise; auto-restart (ms) brings the bus back after a BUS-OFF.
canbus.confirmBitrate: Change the bitrate? The bitrate is fixed in each MCU's firmware - changing it on the host alone will take every CAN MCU offline. Only do this after reflashing every board (and its bootloader) to the same speed. It briefly drops the bus and restarts Klipper. Never during a print.
canbus.confirmParams: Apply these CAN settings? This briefly takes the bus down (every CAN MCU drops), applies the change, brings it back up, then restarts Klipper. Never do this during a print.
canbus.confirmKlipper: Restart Klipper and every MCU now? The CAN MCUs will reconnect. Never do this during a print.
canbus.appliedRestarting: Applied. The bus is back up and Klipper is restarting so the MCUs reconnect.
canbus.restartingKlipper: Klipper is restarting; the MCUs will reconnect.
canbus.restartFailed: The change was applied, but the Klipper restart request failed - restart it manually.
canbus.applyHint: Applying briefly takes the bus down and restarts Klipper so the MCUs reconnect with the new settings.
canbus.advancedTip: Leave Sample point and SJW blank - the kernel picks the recommended ~87.5% sample point automatically. TX queue length should be 128. Auto-restart 0 = off, 100 ms self-recovers from a bus-off.
canbus.flagsWarn: Keep these off for normal printing. Listen-only and One-shot stop the host acknowledging or retrying frames, which makes the MCUs unreachable.

advisor.intro: Host health at a glance — CPU, memory, disk, clock and services, each graded with a fix.

hint.cpu_temp: CPU is running hot. Check cooling and airflow around the board.
hint.cpu_throttled: The board is throttling (under-voltage or heat). Use a known-good PSU/cable and improve cooling.
hint.memory_pressure: Memory is nearly full and swapping. Restart heavy services or add RAM.
hint.disk_full: Disk space is low. Use Cleanup to free caches and old logs.
hint.service_down: A print-stack service is not running. Open Services to start it.
hint.ntp_unsync: The clock isn't synced. Enable NTP in System or set the time.
